questions.question: For which discovery did Einstein receive the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics?

his work on Brownian motion
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that he received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics "for his services to theoretical physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect."
Incorrect. Although Einstein is best known for relativity, the Nobel Prize citation specifically mentioned the photoelectric effect.
Incorrect. The article calls E = mcÂ² "the world's most famous equation," but it was not the reason cited for his Nobel Prize.
Incorrect. Brownian motion is mentioned as one of his 1905 papers, but not as the basis for the Nobel Prize.

questions.question: What did Einstein's 1917 paper introduce that became the core mechanism behind the laser and maser?
options: stimulated emission
spontaneous emission
the cosmological constant
BoseâEinstein statistics
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says his 1917 paper introduced spontaneous and stimulated emission, "the latter of which is the core mechanism behind the laser and maser."
Incorrect. Spontaneous emission was also introduced in the paper, but stimulated emission is identified as the core mechanism behind lasers and masers.
Incorrect. The cosmological constant was introduced in a 1916 paper on general relativity, not the 1917 paper.
Incorrect. BoseâEinstein statistics came from his later collaboration with Satyendra Nath Bose.

questions.question: Which of the following was included in Einstein's annus mirabilis papers of 1905?
options: a demonstration that mass and energy are equivalent if special relativity is correct
a proposal of the general theory of relativity
the introduction of the cosmological constant
the concepts of spontaneous and stimulated emission
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in his 1905 papers he "demonstrated that if the special theory is correct, mass and energy are equivalent to each other."
Incorrect. The general theory of relativity was proposed in 1915, not in 1905.
Incorrect. The cosmological constant appeared in a paper published in 1916.
Incorrect. Spontaneous and stimulated emission were introduced in a 1917 paper.

questions.question: What did Einstein agree to as part of his divorce settlement with Mileva MariÄ?
options: to give her the Nobel Prize money if he won the prize
to return to Zurich and live with her again
to support their sons financially until adulthood
to relinquish his claim to their daughter Lieserl
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says that as part of the divorce settlement, "Einstein agreed that if he were to win a Nobel Prize, he would give the money that he received to MariÄ; he won the prize two years later."
Incorrect. MariÄ returned to Zurich in 1914 and they divorced in 1919; there was no agreement for Einstein to return.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a financial support agreement for their sons in the settlement.
Incorrect. The article does not mention relinquishing any claim to Lieserl as part of the settlement.

questions.question: What did Einstein's father want him to study?
options: electrical engineering
theoretical physics
mathematics
philosophy
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that "His father wanted him to study electrical engineering," but Einstein found the Gymnasium's regimen uncongenial.
Incorrect. Einstein studied physics, but his father specifically wanted him to study electrical engineering.
Incorrect. Although Einstein excelled at mathematics, his father's wish was for electrical engineering.
Incorrect. Einstein read Kant and philosophy, but this was not what his father wanted him to study.

questions.question: What did Einstein object to in quantum theory, famously saying "God does not play dice"?
options: its introduction of fundamental randomness into science's picture of the world
its rejection of the photoelectric effect
its denial of massâenergy equivalence
its reliance on the cosmological constant
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says Einstein "advocated against quantum theory's introduction of fundamental randomness into science's picture of the world, objecting that 'God does not play dice'."
Incorrect. Einstein helped discover the photoelectric effect and did not reject it.
Incorrect. Massâenergy equivalence was Einstein's own result from special relativity.
Incorrect. The cosmological constant was introduced by Einstein himself in general relativity.

questions.question: What did Einstein endorse on the eve of World War II?
options: a letter to President Franklin D. Roosevelt alerting him to the potential German nuclear weapons program
a public statement condemning the Manhattan Project
a petition to the Prussian Academy of Sciences to leave Germany
an application for Swiss citizenship
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that on the eve of World War II, "he endorsed a letter to President Franklin D. Roosevelt alerting him to the potential German nuclear weapons program and recommending that the US begin similar research."
Incorrect. The letter recommended that the US begin similar research, which became the Manhattan Project; he did not condemn it.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a petition to the Prussian Academy.
Incorrect. He had already acquired Swiss citizenship in 1897 and kept it for life.

questions.question: Which institution did Einstein join in Berlin in 1914?
options: the Prussian Academy of Sciences
the Swiss Patent Office
the EidgenÃ¶ssische Technische Hochschule
the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in 1914 he moved to Berlin to join the Prussian Academy of Sciences and Humboldt University of Berlin.
Incorrect. He worked at the Swiss Patent Office in Bern before moving to Berlin.
Incorrect. ETH Zurich is where he enrolled as a student in 1896.
Incorrect. He became director of the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics in 1917, not 1914.

questions.question: What did Einstein's 1916 paper lay out implications for?
options: the modeling of the structure and evolution of the universe as a whole
the photoelectric effect
Brownian motion
the Pythagorean theorem
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says a paper he published in 1916 "laid out the implications of general relativity for the modeling of the structure and evolution of the universe as a whole."
Incorrect. The photoelectric effect was covered in his 1905 annus mirabilis papers.
Incorrect. Brownian motion was also explained in his 1905 papers.
Incorrect. The Pythagorean theorem is mentioned in connection with Einstein's childhood proof, not the 1916 paper.
